transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too, I guess. Well, what brings me in is... I mean, things have just gotten really off lately, specifically with my eating. It's just completely out of whack. Usually, I'm a pretty steady eater, you know? Working in healthcare support, you really need your energy. You're on your feet all day, helping patients, moving around the unit, so you have to fuel up. 

But lately... I don't know, some days I wake up and I barely manage to get down a cup of black coffee and maybe a granola bar before a whole shift. I just stare at food and can't bring myself to eat an actual meal. And it's really starting to show, which is part of why I decided I needed to come in. I put my scrubs on the other morning—the exact same ones I've been wearing for over a year—and they were just hanging loose off me. The waistband was falling down, the top was all baggy around my shoulders... and the thing is, I’m not even trying to lose weight at all. I haven't been on a diet or anything, it's just happening because my appetite is completely gone, and I just can't seem to get it back on track no matter how much I know I need the calories for work. It's just falling off me.
Beyond the loss of appetite, have you been feeling a persistent sense of sadness or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I mean... sadness is one word for it, but it almost feels too small, if that makes sense. It's just... well, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. 

And I mean, my alarm goes off at 5:30 AM, and usually I'd just hop right up, you know? Get the coffee going, maybe listen to the morning news, get my head in the game. But lately, I just sit on the edge of the bed staring at the floor for what feels like twenty, thirty minutes, just feeling this... this crushing weight in my chest. My ID badge is just sitting there on the dresser next to my keys, and I look at it, and I just feel completely empty about the whole thing. 

And it's not just work, either, it's everything. You asked about things I enjoy, and... well, the things I used to actually like doing on my days off are just gone for me. Like, I used to be really into fixing up old electronics, radios and things. I have this whole workbench set up in the spare room, spent a lot of time and money getting it just right over the years—but now I don't even go in there. I just don't care at all. The dust is just collecting on my tools and I can't bring myself to pick them up. It’s just this constant, draining heaviness that follows me everywhere. I try to put on a brave face at the clinic, because, you know, the patients are going through enough and they don't need to see the support staff looking miserable, but it takes every ounce of energy I have just to pretend I'm not completely hollowed out inside.
Have you ever felt this way before in your life, perhaps a few years ago or at another time, or is this the first time you have ever experienced these symptoms?

Well, no, it's not the first time I've ever felt down in my life, obviously, but this specific... this relentless kind of heaviness? It hasn't been a lifelong thing, if that's what you're asking. But it's also not just a recent thing, either. It's actually been going on for a really long time now. 

It all started... gosh, it has to be almost two years ago now. Yeah, two years. That's when the clinic decided to do this massive overhaul of our Electronic Medical Records system—the EMR—and they completely restructured our entire workflow along with it. It was supposed to make everything more "efficient," you know? But what it actually meant was that they completely changed my hours. I went from having this really predictable, steady schedule that I had built my whole life around, to suddenly having these erratic shifts, sometimes early mornings, sometimes late evenings, and it just threw my entire routine into chaos. 

And I remember, at first, I just thought I was tired from the adjustment. You know, learning the new software, trying to figure out the new charting requirements, dealing with the frustrated providers who couldn't figure out how to put in their orders... it was stressful for everyone. But then the stress didn't go away. The new system settled in, everyone else seemed to adapt, but I just... didn't. That's when this hollow feeling really started creeping in. I can almost trace it back to those first few weeks of the new schedule, trying to force myself to care about the new protocols, and just feeling this absolute wall of exhaustion and emptiness hit me. And it just never lifted. It's been almost two years of dragging myself through these shifts, two years of waking up and feeling like I have nothing left to give, two years of my workbench sitting there collecting dust. So, no, it's not brand new, but it's been this one long, continuous slide ever since that whole workflow overhaul upended everything.
In those two years you've been feeling this way, have you had any periods where you felt like yourself again—where the mood and the lack of interest lifted for more than two months at a time?

No, no, I really haven't. And that's... that's the thing that really scares me, honestly. You know, you hear people talk about having a bad month or a rough patch, like maybe around the holidays or when it's dark out in the winter, and then spring comes and they bounce back. But for me, it's just been this one, unbroken, endless stretch of... of just nothingness. 

I keep waiting for it to lift. I kept telling myself, okay, maybe when I finally get used to the new EMR system, I'll feel better. Or maybe when they switch me back to day shifts for a week, I'll snap out of it. I'd even try to force it, you know? Like, I'd go into the spare room, look at my workbench, and say, "Today is the day I'm going to fix that old Zenith radio." I'd even sit down in the chair. But then I'd just sit there for an hour, staring at the vacuum tubes, and I just couldn't make my hands move. The feeling just wouldn't go away. 

There hasn't been a single month, let alone two months, where I woke up and thought, "Hey, I feel like me again." It's just been this constant, low-level dread and exhaustion every single day since the schedule change. Even on my days off, even when I take PTO—which I rarely do anymore because what's the point if I'm just going to sit on the couch?—the heaviness is still right there. It never takes a vacation. It's like I'm stuck at the bottom of a well and I haven't seen the sun in two years, not even for a fleeting second. So, no, there haven't been any breaks in it at all. Not one.
